title: WebSearchTool citation markers incorrectly positioned for multibyte text
body:
### What happened?

The WebSearchTool inserts citation markers (e.g., `[1]`, `[2]`) at incorrect positions when the search response contains multibyte characters such as Japanese text.
The Grounding API returns byte positions for the segments, but the current implementation treats these as character positions, causing markers to appear in the middle of text instead of at the intended locations.

This bug can be reproduced by running a web search query that returns multibyte characters.
https://gist.github.com/pokutuna/e07fe0bbb5c26b419f4fcd89c8800371

---

```
QUERY: Can you suggest Japanese proverbs that effectively express bugs caused by language differences and encoding issues?'

TOOL_RESPONSE:
Web search results for "Can you suggest Japanese proverbs that effectively express bugs caused by language differences and encoding issues?":

Of course. Here are several Japanese proverbs and concepts that can effectively and creatively describe bugs caused by language differences and encoding issues.

...

Here are some proverbs that can be used metaphorically:

**1. 井の中の蛙大海を知らず (I no naka no kawazu taikai o shirazu)**
*   **Literal Translation:** [1][2]"A frog in a well knows nothing of the great ocean."
*   **How it applies:** This powerfully describes the root cause of many internationalization bugs. A developer who has only ever worked with a single language and character set is the "frog in the well." They are unaware of the "great ocean" of different languages, scripts, and encodings, and therefore write code that fails when it encounters them.

**2. 二階から目薬 (Nikai kara megusuri)**
*   **Literal Translation:** "Eyedrops fr[3]om the second floor."
*   **How it applies:** This proverb describes a method that is too roundabout and ultimately ineffective. It's a perfect metaphor for a clumsy attempt to fix an encoding bug without understanding the root cause—for instance, trying to manually replace garbled characters instead of correctly setting the encoding headers. The effort is futile because the approach is fundamentally wrong.

**3. ミイラ取りがミイラになる (Miira tori ga miira ni naru)**
*   **Literal Translation:** "The mummy hunter becomes a mummy."
* [3]  **How it applies:** This humorously describes a developer who dives deep into a complex encoding or internationalization bug. They get so entangled in debugging corrupted data and obscure character sets that their own code becomes a convoluted, unmaintainable mess, effectively "becoming a mummy" themselves.

Sources:
[1] fluentin3months.com (https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGQYPuKiAiJKRzkaWm-5zEr7SCemUtSzR9bQXw1Z8Yba6vF4meuAIOWK-ec2FS7XIf1TGsHQRALEzV_J-kr1yzr5kVUdllS8z6yEtpGSSL5jL_qLV9nw-sOZSWUcsNgnh20DQUu2MiEGatsN9FO)
[2] tandem.net (https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGf6j2itteHi0CdHoWKkMUlCOSctlDEHwaAABTzjb77eDPQsmiYCTnDwhdcfzq-S2gH1eUujJLRrOg5vUHr352ExZcXpsR7eS-rrnlddvJsYO5g_wIfOAZZHz6dZJU9KWBgYB_r)
[3] nihonshock.com (https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFFYpv0TbaxKP-WXPqb69gQ917bzS0oMyFTRor397JRi8EKnh0qOy17iHWtbUlJNqiTyBjQ9hpkfIER5-5KSrpi2clPfS22WAIPB0VuLso3i04TjDnplKFHllIZWAj2cSGhIN6bRQj2jX4_Vi0NJIATPg2R23jtwmn7)
```


### What did you expect to happen?

Citation markers should be inserted at the correct positions as intended by the API response, appearing at natural text boundaries (e.g., word endings, sentence endings) rather than mid-word or within formatting.

### Client information

<details>

```console
$ gemini /about
╭─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                     │
│ About Gemini CLI                                                    │
│                                                                     │
│ CLI Version             0.1.18                                      │
│ Git Commit              cd7e60e0                                    │
│ Model                   gemini-2.5-pro                              │
│ Sandbox                 no sandbox                                  │
│ OS                      darwin                                      │
│ Auth Method             vertex-ai                                   │
│ GCP Project             pokutuna-playground                           │
│                                                                     │
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

</details>


### Login information

Reproduces with both Vertex AI and API key authentication methods.

### Anything else we need to know?

While users may rarely see malformed output since Gemini likely removes unnatural citations from tool responses, avoiding corrupted input to the LLM is still beneficial for improving output quality and citation preservation.

In `packages/core/src/tools/web-search.ts`,  the code uses `modifiedResponseText.split('')` to create a character array and then uses `splice()` with byte indices from the API response. This causes incorrect positioning when multibyte UTF-8 characters are present, as JavaScript's `split('')` operates on Unicode code points while the API provides byte offsets.


These documents show that the startIndex and endIndex of the segment are byte positions.
- [Gemini API Segment](https://ai.google.dev/api/generate-content#Segment)
- [Vertex AI GroundingSupport](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1beta1/GroundingMetadata#GroundingSupport)

Although the encoding of the target text is not explicitly specified, it would be reasonable to consider it as UTF-8. When I made modifications to handle it as UTF-8, the marker positions became natural.

linked_prs.title: fix(core): citation markers misplaced in search results containing multibyte characters
linked_prs.body:
## TLDR

Fixes incorrect positioning of citation markers in WebSearchTool when responses contain multibyte characters by properly handling byte positions from the Gemini API instead of treating them as character positions.


## Dive Deeper

The WebSearchTool was incorrectly inserting citation markers when dealing with multibyte UTF-8 characters (such as Japanese text). The Gemini API returns grounding segment positions as byte offsets, but the previous implementation used JavaScript's string splitting which operates on Unicode code points, causing markers to appear in wrong locations.

**Changes made:**
1. **Fixed marker insertion logic** in `packages/core/src/tools/web-search.ts`:
   - Replaced character-based string manipulation with TextEncoder/TextDecoder
   - Use browser-compatible TextEncoder/TextDecoder for byte position handling
   - Maintain proper UTF-8 encoding throughout the process

2. **Added new test file** `packages/core/src/tools/web-search.test.ts`:
   - WebSearchTool previously had no dedicated test coverage
   - Added basic functionality tests for citation marker insertion
   - Includes test cases for multibyte character handling scenarios
   - Ensures markers are placed at correct byte boundaries

The fix ensures backward compatibility and cross-platform support (Node.js and browsers) while correctly handling all UTF-8 text, including ASCII-only content.

While users may rarely see malformed output since Gemini likely removes unnatural citations from tool responses, this fix improves LLM input quality and citation preservation.

## Reviewer Test Plan

- Please review the test execution and citation insertion logic
- After receiving this tool response, Gemini will likely fix any unnatural citations in the text, so it will be difficult to obtain broken output via CLI.
  - By having the marker positions be correct, subsequent outputs using WebSearchTool are expected to become more accurate. However, it is difficult to confirm this deterministically.
